Early marks are interpreted either as abstract signs of smallness or as fine sand grains; their referent remains disputed.","evidence_ids":["ref013","ref014","ref018","ref026","ref033","ref035","ref006","ref007"]}

{"text":"小 has no settled account of what its early marks represent: analyses describe abstract signs of smallness, raindrops or scattered objects, or fine sand grains. The sand-grain account treats 小 as an early graph of 沙, but neither the depicted referent nor a sound-based borrowing is established. Accounts also describe 小 and 少 as sharing an early graph before they were differentiated; one account says 少’s lower dot became a diagonal stroke. In small-seal script, the central dot became a vertical stroke between two side marks. Shuowen’s analysis of this later form as 八 plus 丨 is a historical interpretation, not evidence of the original construction.","evidence_ids":["ref003","ref013","ref014","ref016","ref017","ref018","ref020","ref024","ref025","ref032","ref033","ref034","ref035","ref042"]}

{"text":"Shuowen parses the seal form as 八 and 丨, explaining the marks as dividing something. Later analyses treat this as a reinterpretation of an altered form. Accounts also describe 小 and 少 as once sharing a graph before later differentiation, though their detailed graphic and lexical relationship remains unsettled.","evidence_ids":["ref003","ref004","ref016","ref017","ref018","ref019","ref035","ref042"]}
